description: key-hierarchy design §5.6 fork resolution as trees (KH1): each case is a tree of verified epochs (ids, authors, lists and computed removals as labels; a label stands for its UTF-8 bytes, so epochId order is byte order), what the device brings (me, its stored answers, addedBy chains, its pinned chain); each node carries its recovery fingerprint, and the expected kept chain, losses (child, winner, rule), re-application set, open question and contradictions. Scenarios from design §11.1.

cases.name: honest concurrent removals: rule 4 and re-application
two re-appliers at once: the second finds nothing left to remove
honest fork at a non-frontier level: rule 3, keys removed after the branch stay removed
removed X forks from an older epoch with a ground epochId and descendants: rule 1 over the subtree
mutual removal: a non-author device is asked, names from the parent list
mutual removal answered: the rejected author loses (rule 2), nothing re-applied
mutual removal, no answer yet: an author keeps its own side (A)
mutual removal, no answer yet: an author keeps its own side (X)
a resolve epoch by a founder binds the authors (X follows it)
a resolve epoch does not bind a non-author: it is still asked, with the resolve as context
a puppet's resolve (N, added by X) does not bind the authors: A keeps its side
a puppet's resolve does not bind X either: X keeps its own side; a non-author is asked
a resolve by a device added after the branch (D, approved by C) binds the authors
a device added after the branch is among those asked
three children: the pre-pass discards X's ground-id fork (rule 1), no question, B's stale side is re-applied
a rejected author's later forks lose without asking again
contradicting answers: the device follows its own and reports the resolve epoch
a losing recovery replacement: its removal of the old recovery key is never re-applied
review C1: X appends to an old honest stale fork; its epoch counts for nothing (me A)
review C1: X appends to an old honest stale fork; its epoch counts for nothing (me B)
review C1: X appends to an old honest stale fork; its epoch counts for nothing (me C)
review C1 variant: X appends to the old stale fork and removes every third device too
review C1 variant: the stale fork is still re-applied when the kept chain has not removed Y
pinned context: a device that pinned the removal of X never sees X fork from before it
pruning: an epoch whose author the kept prefix removed does not continue it
review M4: two binding resolve epochs that disagree are a contradiction and a question (me A)
review M4: two binding resolve epochs that disagree are a contradiction and a question (me X)
review L3: X removes every other device: mutual with the remover, a question
